proof:
# Four simplex fibers: an all-dimensional ordered-endpoint peak case

Let T be the standard d-simplex, V=|T|, d>=2, and
Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d. Suppose the four actual integer fibers, at bases
0,1,2,3, are positively homothetic copies of T with positive concave
radii

    (a,b,1,c),  0<a<=2b-1,  1/2<b<=c<=1.                 (1)

Then the own-fiber centroid at base 2 has absolute mixed cap depth
at least

    (Gamma/2)(a^d+b^d+1+c^d)V.                           (2)

For common-vertex fibers the selected point is (2,g_T). For arbitrary
compatible translations, the same conclusion holds at the actual
base-2 centroid, by the independently proved own-centroid comparison
in `candidate 24467ade6f021ae8`.
Thus the normalized depth is at least Gamma/2. This result treats
the ordered-endpoint peak case c>=b, not every four-fiber profile.

The proof uses only the older subset coefficient 1/2. In particular,
it also verifies the proposed stronger lambda_d certificate on (1),
since the sharp subset coefficient is at least 1/2.

## 1. One actual all-cap payment

Put g=(1/(d+1),...,1/(d+1)) and K=T-g. Retain the triple at bases
1,2,3, and write its local base as z=-1,0,1. The affine shear

    x'=x-g-z(c-1)g

turns these three fibers into

    A'=bK+(b+c-2)g,  K,  cK.                            (3)

After adding cg to both A' and cK, they become

    bT-eta*1,  cT,  eta=2(1-c)/(d+1).

Their intersection, when it has positive volume, is exactly hT,
where

    h=[b-(2d/(d+1))(1-c)]_+.                            (4)

Indeed intersection points have nonnegative coordinates and coordinate
sum at most b-d eta<=b<=c. Thus E=hT-cg is an actual subset of
A' and cK. If h=0, use the empty subset; any residual lower-dimensional
intersection has zero d-volume.

The proved measurable-subset theorem in
`candidate dafd411c026c302c` gives
at the middle centroid, for every nonvertical ambient through-cap,

    cap(E,cK,cK) >= Gamma*c^d*V + (1/2)h^d*V.

The unused part of the actual central K contributes exactly
(1-c^d) times the central cap of K, and therefore at least
Gamma(1-c^d)V. The fourth fiber contributes nonnegative mass. Hence
every such actual cap has mass at least

    [Gamma+(1/2)h^d]V.                                  (5)

This retains one continuous normal and one base tilt. No independently
minimized fiber profiles have been added. A closed vertical cap through
base 2 contains the whole central fiber and at least one neighboring
fiber. Its mass is at least (1+b^d)V, which exceeds (5), since
h<=b and Gamma<1. Every containing halfspace contains a parallel
through-halfspace. Thus (5) is an all-halfspace lower bound.

## 2. The scalar inequality

We prove for every integer d>=2 and 1/2<=b<=c<=1 that

    1+[(1+1/d)b+2c-2]_+^d
      >= (2b-1)^d+b^d+c^d.                              (6)

Since (1+1/d)^d=1/Gamma and
[(1+1/d)b+2c-2]_+=(1+1/d)h, multiplying (6) by Gamma/2 gives

    Gamma+(1/2)h^d
      >= (Gamma/2)[1+(2b-1)^d+b^d+c^d].                 (7)

The upper bound a<=2b-1 finishes (2).

Write s=1+1/d and

    F(b,c)=1+[s b+2c-2]_+^d-(2b-1)^d-b^d-c^d.

For fixed b, before the positive-part term turns on the derivative
with respect to c is negative. Afterwards its sign is the sign of

    2(s b+2c-2)^(d-1)-c^(d-1).

Set q=2^(-1/(d-1)). The ratio (s b+2c-2)/c is strictly increasing
in c, since 2-sb>0. Therefore the only possible interior minimum is

    c_*(b)=(2-sb)/(2-q),

where s b+2c_*-2=q c_*. Its value is

    F_*(b)=1-(2b-1)^d-b^d
             -(2-sb)^d/[2(2-q)^(d-1)].                 (8)

This is a concave function of b on [1/2,1]. The feasible critical
branch b<=c_*(b)<=1 is precisely

    I=[max(1/2,q/s), 2/(s+2-q)].                        (9)

It is a nonempty closed interval: q/s<=2/(s+2-q) follows from
(q-2)(s-q)<=0, and its upper endpoint is at least 1/2 and at most 1.
The right endpoint has c_*=b. The left endpoint has either c_*=1
or b=1/2. Concavity of (8) now reduces the complete minimum problem
to the three boundary edges c=1, c=b, and b=1/2. The following
checks include the positive-part regime and all endpoints.

For c=1,

    F(b,1)=(s^d-1)b^d-(2b-1)^d>=0,

because 0<=2b-1<=b and s^d>=2 by Bernoulli's inequality.

For c=b, divide F(b,b)>=0 by b^d and put u=1/b-1 in [0,1].
The required inequality is

    (1+u)^d-(1-u)^d+[1+1/d-2u]_+^d>=2.

The odd terms in the binomial difference give a lower bound 2du.
With v=2du it remains to show

    v+[1+(1-v)/d]_+^d>=2.                               (10)

If v<=d+1, Bernoulli's inequality gives the power term at least
2-v. If v>=d+1, the left side is v>=3. This proves (10) on the
entire required range.

For b=1/2 and d>=3, q>=1/sqrt(2)>2/3>=s/2. Hence
c_*(1/2)>=1 and F(1/2,c) is nonincreasing up to c=1; the already
proved c=1 bound applies. For d=2,

    F(1/2,c)=3/4+[2c-5/4]_+^2-c^2.

On c<=5/8 this is at least 23/64. On c>=5/8 it equals

    3(c-5/6)^2+11/48>0.

This finishes (6) and the theorem.

## 3. Verification and scope

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_four_simplex_ordered_peak_and_monotone_gap.py` checks (6)
with exact rational arithmetic in several dimensions, verifies its
scalar transformations and the d=2 boundary identity, and independently
checks the exact monotone obstruction in the companion note. These
checks supplement the all-dimensional proof; they do not establish it.

The other peak order c<b remains outside this note. The result neither
classifies critical bodies nor establishes a general four-fiber theorem
in dimensions d>=3. In dimension 2 the other order is already settled
by `candidate 86b03c88b3643f55`.
